blocks.content:
Turn a team procedure into a guide that a colleague can follow inside Grafana. Build a small practice guide with text, recorded actions, and an explanation of a page control.

**You need:** Editor or Admin access. No dashboards, data sources, or integrations are required. Allow about 15 minutes.

Keep these instructions floating beside the editor. Drag this window away from a control when necessary.

**Protect existing work:** Use an empty practice guide. If the editor contains another guide, save or download it first. Then choose **More actions → New guide**. Opening this lesson does not replace your work.

blocks.title: Explain the task to your reader

blocks.content:
Imagine that your team needs a short guide for new colleagues: find dashboards by name. Start with the outcome, not a list of Grafana features.

Use the example values in this lesson. Later, adapt the guide to your team's names and procedures. **Do it** enters the example. **Show me** points to the control.
Name the practice guide **Find your team's dashboards**.
blocks.tooltip: Use a title that describes what the reader will accomplish.

blocks.content: Add a short introduction with a **Markdown** block. Explain when a colleague needs this guide.

steps.description: Choose Add block.
Choose Markdown.
Choose Raw to enter Markdown text.

steps.targetvalue: Use this guide when you need a dashboard for your team's service. Search by a service or dashboard name. An empty result means that no visible dashboard matches your search.
steps.description: Enter a short introduction. For example: Use this guide to find dashboards for your team's service. Search by service or dashboard name.
Add the Markdown block.

blocks.content: The introduction adds context rather than repeating the title. For a company guide, link to the authoritative runbook or standard instead of copying a long document.

A section groups the steps for one activity. Here, the activity is a dashboard search.

**Recording captures live actions, not video.** Recorded clicks and input affect your current stack. This exercise only changes a search filter.
Open **Dashboards** before recording.
Create a section named **Search the dashboard list**, then start recording into it.

steps.description: Choose Add block.
Choose Section.
Enter Search the dashboard list as the section title. Keep the generated section ID.
Choose Add and record. The recording toolbar will appear.

blocks.content: No matching dashboards? That is fine. The exercise uses the search control, not any existing dashboard.
Record the search, then stop the recording.

steps.description: Enter team in the dashboard search field. Then press Tab to capture the input.
Press Tab to finish the input. After the toolbar reports 1 block, choose Stop.

blocks.content: Recording supplies a starting point, not a finished explanation. Give the search action a useful instruction and a page requirement.
Improve the recorded search action. Follow the highlighted controls into its editor form.

steps.description: Edit the recorded search action inside Search the dashboard list.

steps.targetvalue: Search for a service or dashboard name. Try team for this practice guide.
steps.description: Replace the description with: Search for a service or dashboard name. Try team for this practice guide.
Choose Test. Check that the highlight identifies the dashboard search field.
Select the suggested on-page:/dashboards requirement. This requirement keeps the action on the Dashboards page.
Choose Update block to keep your instruction and page requirement.

blocks.content:
Prefer built-in **grafana:** selectors or selectors based on **data-testid**, accessible names, and stable attributes. Long class names and numbered positions can break after a UI change.

For longer procedures, use one interactive block per action. Use a **Guided** block when the reader must perform a sequence.
Not every step needs automation. Add a show-only highlight that explains what the dashboard search can find.
Pick the search field, explain it, and give the reader a Show me button without a Do it button.

steps.description: Add a block inside Search the dashboard list.
Choose Interactive. Keep the default Highlight action.
Choose Pick element. Next, select the center of the dashboard search field, away from its icon.

steps.targetvalue: This search matches dashboards and folders that you can access. An empty result can mean that you need a different name or more permissions.
steps.description: Enter: This search matches dashboards and folders that you can access. An empty result can mean that you need a different name or more permissions.
Choose Test. Check that the selected target is the search field, not its icon.
Clear Show 'Do it' button. Keep Show 'Show me' button selected.
Add the explanatory highlight to your section.

blocks.content: The element picker captures a selector. **Test** helps you check its target. **exists-reftarget** prevents the step from running without that target.
Preview uses the live Grafana page. Try the action and the explanation as your colleague will see them.
Prepare a clean search, then open your guide in Preview.

steps.description: Clear the dashboard search filter. Your recorded action will enter the search term again.
Select Preview to read your guide without the editor forms.

blocks.content:
In Preview, try **Show me** on your search action to check its target. Use **Do it** to enter **team** again.

Try **Show me** on the explanation. It must have no **Do it** button.

Return to **Edit** after the check. If you repeat the check, use **Reset guide** in Preview first.

Before you share a company guide, ask a colleague to try it with the intended reader's permissions. An Admin test does not prove that a Viewer can complete it.

Check resource access, links, and any values that can expose sensitive information.

blocks.title: Save a draft, not a practice publication

blocks.content:
The editor automatically keeps your current work in this browser. **Save** also stores a draft in the guide library when the backend is available.

Return to **Edit** before saving. Keep this exercise as a draft. You do not need to publish it to complete the lesson.
Choose **Save** to store the practice guide as a draft.
blocks.tooltip: A draft is not a published guide for your colleagues.
blocks.hint: If Save is unavailable, use More actions → Download JSON to keep a separate copy.

blocks.content: Open a separate JSON copy of your practice guide.

steps.description: Open More actions to find the export controls.
Choose Download JSON to open a JSON copy in a new browser tab. Your guide stays unpublished.

blocks.content:
Save the JSON copy from your browser to keep it as a file.

After a server save, check that the editor shows **Draft**. You can reopen server-saved guides through **More actions → Library**.

For your first company guide, replace the sample with one real team procedure. Add links to your standards. Ask a colleague to try it before you publish.

When Grafana or your procedure changes, reopen the guide and repeat the Preview test. Recording does not maintain the guide for you.
